issue: Is the 30-day filing deadline in 8 U.S.C. § 1252(b)(1) for petitions for review of immigration orders a mandatory claim-processing rule that must be enforced when properly raised, so that equitable tolling is unavailable?

sides.position: The § 1252(b)(1) thirty-day filing rule is a mandatory claim-processing rule that, if properly raised, must be enforced, leaving no room for equitable tolling.
cases: Jaime Navarro Cerritos v. Todd Blanche, No. 23-1897 (4th Cir. 2026)

this_court: Holds the thirty-day deadline in § 1252(b)(1) is mandatory and not subject to equitable tolling, and openly acknowledges that this deepens a split with other circuits.
quote: conclude[d] that § 1252(b)(1)’s thirty-day filing rule is a mandatory claim-processing rule that, if properly raised, must be enforced.
cite: Jaime Navarro Cerritos v. Todd Blanche, No. 23-1897 (4th Cir. 2026)
